newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Commerzbank CEO says unworried by Bonn gold project.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank CEO says unworried by Bonn gold project.

text.p: Commerzbank AG chief excecutive Martin Kohlhaussen said on Tuesday he was unconcerned by Bonn's controversial plans to revalue gold and currency reserves to help meet European currency union goals.
"This is nothing special," Kohlhaussen told Reuters Financial Television.
"The gold is valued at very very low prices. I would not mind a revaluation," he added.
Kohlhaussen said he fully expected the government to come to an agreement on the issue with the Bundesbank, after the German central bank rejected Bonn's plans as an infringement on its autonomy.
"This is an important issue which should be discussed. But I am pretty sure the government is not interested in hurting the reputation of the Bundesbank or the other way around."

Kohlhaussen was speaking on the fringes of the International Monetary Conference in Switzerland, at which German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Monday defended his gold revaluation plan before an audience of more than 100 top bankers.

The Bundesbank has rejected as an infringement of its autonomy Bonn's revaluation plan, which envisages a transfer to the state this year and next of extraordinary profits generated from revaluing assets at the Bundesbank closer to market values.
Bonn has said it wants to use the procedure to retire old debt.

The Commerzbank chief added that he continued to favour monetary union starting with as large a group of countries as possible. He said significant progress had been made in the European Union toward harmonising fiscal and inflation positions.

But he also said he did not expect a dramatic market reaction should monetary union have to be delayed, as has been increasingly suggested after the Bonn-Bundesbank dispute and Socialist Party victory in France.
"Markets are always volatile. But we should not dramatise the situation," Kohlhaussen said.
Kohlhaussen added that he considered a dollar-mark exchange rate of 1.70 to 1.72 marks to be "an appropriate rate."
